title: Phase 1 Portfolio flip-card interaction correctness + hover resilience + object URL cleanup

requirements.summary: Eliminate overlapping flip triggers so Portfolio flip-cards toggle exactly once per user action (mouse + keyboard) and lightbox actions do not affect flip state.
acceptanceCriteria: On the public Portfolio page, clicking a photo flips the card exactly once per click (no immediate flip-back or double flip).
On the public Portfolio page, clicking a video pauses it and flips to the back showing the description; clicking again flips back to the front; the state changes exactly once per click.
Clicking the “View Full” button on the flip-card back opens the lightbox and does not change the flip state.
Keyboard interaction (Enter/Space) flips exactly once and follows the same rules as mouse click.

file_operations.description: Adjust FlipCard interaction plumbing so there is a single, predictable flip trigger per user action (click + Enter/Space), avoiding double-toggles when nested children also handle clicks; keep it compatible with controlled flipping via isFlipped/onFlippedChange.

Refactor PortfolioGrid flip logic to remove overlapping click handlers between inner front/back content and the FlipCard container; ensure the 'View Full' button prevents flip state changes (stopPropagation + trigger detection) and that video-specific pause-on-flip behavior is applied exactly once per interaction.

requirements.summary: Make video hover autoplay/pause behavior match the specified rules and remain stable when autoplay is blocked by the browser.
acceptanceCriteria: When hovering a video flip-card front, the video attempts to autoplay; when unhovering, it pauses.
When a video card is flipped to the back, hover does not start playback until the card is flipped back to the front.
If the browser blocks autoplay, the UI remains functional (no crashes, no infinite error toasts); the video remains paused and can still be flipped via click.

file_operations.description: Harden video hover behavior: only attempt playback when the card is currently on the front; pause reliably on unhover and on flip-to-back; guard play() calls to tolerate autoplay promise rejections without surfacing noisy UI errors and without breaking flip interactions.

Ensure keyboard/click flipping behavior remains consistent while allowing PortfolioGrid to prevent unintended hover-driven playback when the card is flipped (e.g., by enabling the parent to conditionally disable pointer interactions on the front side while flipped).

requirements.summary: Revoke object URLs for Portfolio media previews (grid + lightbox) to prevent memory leaks during repeated browsing.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigating into and out of the Portfolio page repeatedly does not continuously increase memory usage due to unreleased object URLs.
Object URLs created for grid thumbnails and the lightbox media are revoked when no longer needed (e.g., component unmount or item change).
No broken images/videos appear due to premature revocation (revocation only occurs after the media is no longer displayed).

file_operations.description: Add a small utility (and/or hook helpers) for creating object URLs from bytes and revoking them safely during React lifecycle transitions (unmount, item change), ensuring revocation happens only after the consuming element no longer needs the URL.

Replace per-render URL.createObjectURL calls with memoized/object-url-managed URLs per item (keyed by item id + media kind/bytes identity), and revoke URLs when items change or the grid unmounts to prevent leaks while avoiding premature revocation.

Stop creating a new object URL every render; instead create a managed URL for the currently viewed item and revoke it when the lightbox closes or the item changes, ensuring no broken media during viewing.

Ensure the lightbox mounts/unmounts (or item changes) in a way that triggers object URL cleanup paths in the lightbox component during close and navigation, preventing retained URLs across repeated Portfolio visits.
